parsed.explanation: No traveler-facing restriction is documented: entry accepts foreign passports, no trans-specific offence, no facility or custody rule, no police targeting or profiling of trans visitors. The negatives are climate-level: a hostile social climate by regional standards, one lethal attack on an LGBT venue (a single incident whose primary target was the prime minister, not a pattern of trans-specific violence), a regressive legislative wave (bills failed, including one that would have criminalised transition — a latent hostile effort, not law), a revoked care-standards episode, and hate-crime law covering sexual orientation more explicitly than gender identity. Anti-discrimination law covering gender identity in goods and services provides theoretical recourse in a functioning rule-of-law state; no evidence shows it failing trans visitors specifically. Societal hostility with thin-but-existing recourse and volatile support places this at reduced risk, but the documented hostility, lethal incident aftermath and legislative trajectory hold it below the acceptance-and-working-protection tier — comparable to a 0.65 profile with weaker social acceptance.
